children: Our Bureau New Delhi: SpiceJet has called a board meeting on November 18 to consider raising fresh capital through equity, preferential shares or debt as the cash-strapped airline grapples with mounting dues and shrinking operations that threaten its ability to avoid being grounded. The board would look at fundraising through a preferential issue, qualified institutional placement (QIP) or any other route approved by the board, SpiceJet informed stock exchanges on Friday.

A few potential investors have already shown interest, people familiar with the development said, although airline has not disclosed any details of prospective investments. The fundraising move comes at a critical juncture for SpiceJet, which has seen its operations shrink sharply amid difficulties in meeting payments to airports, suppliers and other service providers.

Its international operations have been particularly affected. Dnata, the ground-handling services provider at Dubai airport, stopped allocating check-in counters to SpiceJet over unpaid dues estimated at around 35 crore, leading to cancellations of flights. The airline, which operated around 75 weekly flights to Dubai a few months ago, has since sharply reduced its operations on the route.

SpiceJet has also failed to meet the statutory 45-day payment deadline on more than 85% of invoices from small suppliers, with 63.03 crore remaining unpaid beyond the stipulated period between April and September, according to a report by The Tribune. The airline's domestic market share halved in one month to 0.6% in September from 1.2% in August, according to the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA).

Its on-time performance stood at just 16.6% in September, compared with 91.1% for IndiGo and 90.8% for Akasa Air, according to the regulator's data. SpiceJet has been forced to curtail flights as aircraft availability and financial constraints weigh on its schedule. title: SpiceJet Calls Board Meeting to Discuss Fresh Fundraising Plans
